c.text: DECEMBER 1915
On the Russian front, a German army lieutenant...
...worked out the paths of artillery shells
His name was Karl Schwarzschild...
One of Germany's most famous astronomers
Amid the noise of war...
EINSTEIN'S GENERAL RELATIVITY
...he found the first exact solution of its equations
Einstein himself was amazed
But the solution hid a strange boundary
If all of an object's mass is squeezed into a small ball...
...nothing can ever come back out of it
Not even light
For the Sun, that ball would be just 6 km wide
For Earth, the size of a marble
Five months later, Schwarzschild was dead
He never knew what his calculation was hiding...
BLACK HOLE
More than 100 years later...
The James Webb Space Telescope found a black hole...
...that may be older than its own galaxy

c.text: Near a black hole, gravity isn't just strong
It isn't even, either
Whatever part of a falling object is closer to the black hole is pulled much harder
The object gets longer and thinner, like spaghetti
Scientists call it exactly that... spaghettification
SPAGHETTIFICATION
Seen from far away, a falling object slows down near the event horizon, as if time itself stopped
Its light turns red, then dim, and finally disappears
In 2019, this stopped being just an idea
About 210 million light-years away, a Sun-like star passed very close to a supermassive black hole
The black hole tore it into a long stream and swallowed about half its mass
Telescopes including Chile's Very Large Telescope recorded this death for six months
A star had never been seen dying like this, so close
